title: Anthropic's ‘watermark’ text adulteration in Claude is a perversion of writing
titleZh: Anthropic在《克劳德》中的“水印”文本掺假是对写作的歪曲
author: ropbear
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: When I wrote this week about Anthropic’s announcement that all Claude models, worldwide, would soon begin “watermarking” everything they generate, including text, to comply with this EU regulation, we were left to speculate how this was going to work, because Anthropic offered not even a vague description of how it would work — despite the fact that the title of the announcement was, absurdly and insultingly, “How Claude Marks AI-Generated Content”.

My initial speculation was that maybe they’d hide invisible non-printing Unicode characters in the text. Just spitballing. Turns out that’s not what they’re going to do. What they’re going to do is apply a form of steganography, where the choice of words (or other token output) at inference time will leave fingerprints that can later, maybe, be detected probabilistically.

I initially guessed “invisible characters” not because I didn’t think of the semantic word-choice technique, but because I was a fool who took Anthropic at its word in their description of what they would do. Their original support document claims:

When a supported Claude model generates text, it weaves an imperceptible watermark directly into the text itself. You won’t see it, and it doesn’t change the meaning, quality, or readability of Claude’s response.

They say “imperceptible” and “doesn’t change the meaning, quality, or readability”. Their words. Not almost imperceptible. Not slightly changes the meaning, quality, or readability. That made sense to me, because that’s absolutely what I want — nay, demand — from any tools I use personally. It’s unacceptable for a tool to sacrifice an iota of clarity, coherence, meaning, quality, etc. for the purpose of embedding hidden clues within the text to suggest its provenance. That’s what I would and will demand. And Anthropic’s (original) support document unambiguously claims that’s what their system will enable. So if that were true, I couldn’t see what was left other than hiding invisible characters within the text.

comments.author: ghrl
comments.textRawHtml:
My biggest concern is that checking any text for watermarks requires sending the entire text to Anthropic. And even that is not sufficient, as the text might have been generated with ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Mistral, ...

So every check requires sending the text to as many AI providers as offer a watermarking detection API, almost all of which have a very dubious track history with obtaining training data through illicit means.

Any university using AI detection in their submission pipeline, or lawyers, editorialists, proofreaders that check for AI marks will be sending significant amounts of text like unpublished research, books, potentially internal documents and more, most of which is high quality human written, to dozens of AI companies, blindly trusting they won't train on any of that.
comments.textZhHtml:
我最担心的是检查任何文本是否有水印需要将整个文本发送到 Anthropic。即使这还不够，因为文本可能是用 ChatGPT、Gemini、Grok、Mistral 生成的……

因此，每次检查都需要将文本发送给提供水印检测 API 的尽可能多的 AI 提供商，几乎所有这些提供商都有通过非法手段获取训练数据的非常可疑的历史记录。

任何在提交管道中使用 AI 检测的大学，或检查 AI 标记的律师、编辑、校对员都将发送文本向数十家人工智能公司提供大量文本，例如未发表的研究、书籍、潜在的内部文档等，其中大部分是高质量的人类编写的文本，盲目地相信他们不会对这些内容进行培训。

children.author: ThePhysicist
children.textRawHtml: Would really like to know how their watermarking technique works, and if they can use it to store arbitrary information in the text (I assume they can if only in a limited way). I assume if the text is long enough they could add all kinds of metadata that would then be undetectable as the model that generated the text is the "cryptographic" key that encodes the data. I wonder if you can have another model run over the text and destroy the watermark. I predict an interesting cat and mouse game to develop.
children.textZhHtml: 真的很想知道他们的水印技术是如何工作的，以及他们是否可以使用它来存储文本中的任意信息（我认为他们可以，但只能以有限的方式）。我假设如果文本足够长，他们可以添加各种元数据，这些元数据将无法检测到，因为生成文本的模型是对数据进行编码的“加密”密钥。我想知道你是否可以让另一个模型运行文本并销毁水印。我预计将会开发出一款有趣的猫捉老鼠游戏。

children.author: unbelievr
children.textRawHtml:
The paper for it is open. The technique isn't really hiding information in the text itself, but by forcing some of the rolls to follow a specific pattern. LLMs work by estimating the most likely next token, so there's sometimes a list of possible candidates that would all work in the text (e.g. synonyms). At low "temperature", the output is a bit more deterministic and otherwise it's a weighted dice roll of which token/word to pick. An LLM can loop over existing text and figure out if the output matches something it would do, similar to checking chess moves against the best computed move for detecting cheating. But the LLM purposefully creates a pattern of alternating weighted rolls that are highly unlikely to appear in normal text, and that becomes the watermarking.

The upside is that this has very low false positive detection rate, but the downsides are many. It only works on longer pieces of text. The system is fragile, and small edits (or rewrites by a local model) can fool the detection. Only the owner of the model is able to re-run inference at this level, so data must be sent to them for evaluation. And sometimes the token output is basically 100% deterministic because the input asks for the straight answer to a fact, or to recite a quote verbatim. That leaves no room for watermarking at all, unless the model is able to lie.
children.textZhHtml:
其论文已公开。该技术并不是真正将信息隐藏在文本本身中，而是通过强制某些卷遵循特定的模式。法学硕士通过估计最有可能的下一个标记来工作，因此有时会出现一个可能在文本中起作用的候选者列表（例如同义词）。在低“温度”下，输出更具确定性，否则它是选择哪个标记/单词的加权骰子。 LLM 可以循环现有文本并确定输出是否与它会执行的操作相匹配，类似于根据最佳计算的棋步检查国际象棋棋步以检测作弊。但法学硕士有目的地创建了一种极不可能出现在普通文本中的交替加权滚动模式，这就是水印。

优点是误报检测率非常低，但缺点也很多。它仅适用于较长的文本。该系统很脆弱，小的编辑（或本地模型的重写）可能会欺骗检测。只有模型的所有者才能在此级别重新运行推理，因此必须将数据发送给他们进行评估。有时，令牌输出基本上是 100% 确定性的，因为输入要求对事实进行直接回答，或者逐字背诵引文。除非模型能够撒谎，否则根本没有水印的空间。

children.author: vintermann
children.textRawHtml:
A way to think of it is that any time the model faces a choice, it leaks some fractional bits of information. Instead of making the choice randomly, you can put information in those bits.

But unless you know the prompt, you don't fully know which choice the model faces. Surely a lot of coding space is wasted compensating for that uncertainty. Exotic prompts ("Use no more than five E's in four consecutive words anywhere in the text") seem like they will confuse the hell out of attempts to extract the bits from the output text alone.
children.textZhHtml:
一种思考方式是，每当模型面临选择时，它都会泄漏一些小数位信息。您可以将信息放入这些位中，而不是随机做出选择。

但是除非您知道提示，否则您不完全知道模型面临哪个选择。当然，为了补偿这种不确定性，大量的编码空间被浪费了。异国情调的提示（“在文本中的任何位置的四个连续单词中使用不超过五个 E”）似乎会使单独从输出文本中提取位的尝试感到困惑。

children.author: Majromax
children.textRawHtml:
> But unless you know the prompt, you don't fully know which choice the model faces. Surely a lot of coding space is wasted compensating for that uncertainty.

When you only need to encode one bit, the signal to noise ratio can be very low. If I try to write my own human words under the policy of "try a little bit to avoid the letter 'e' in every fifth word," then a sufficiently long text would still be 'watermarked' even if I only succeed in this dictum (e.g.) 10% more often than the baseline.
children.textZhHtml:
> 但除非你知道提示，否则你并不完全知道模型面临哪个选择。当然，为了补偿这种不确定性，会浪费大量编码空间。

当您只需要编码一位时，信噪比可能会非常低。 如果我尝试按照“尽量避免每五个单词中出现字母“e””的策略来写自己的人类单词，那么即使我在这个格言中成功的次数（例如）仅比基线多 10%，足够长的文本仍然会被“加水印”。

children.author: applicative
children.textRawHtml: In fact such ‘arbitrary’ constraints uniformly improve composition.  Thus eg if I force a - largely arbitrary - technical glossary to be unrelentingly applied to a translation, every single sentence improves in quality.
children.textZhHtml: 事实上，这种“任意”约束一致地改善了组合。  因此，例如，如果我强制将一个（很大程度上是任意的）技术术语表不懈地应用于翻译，那么每个句子的质量都会提高。

children.author: demibabs
children.textRawHtml:
> The system is fragile, and small edits (or rewrites by a local model) can fool the detection.

Well no, small edits wouldn’t fool the detection as long as the seeding only uses a small run of previous tokens.

And yeah full rewrites breaking it is by design. The watermark is just meant to tell you whether the text was generated by a watermarked model, not whether the ideas came from AI or something like that.
children.textZhHtml:
> 系统很脆弱，小的编辑（或本地模型的重写）可能会欺骗检测。

好吧，不，只要播种仅使用一小部分先前的令牌，小的编辑就不会欺骗检测。

是的，完全重写破坏它是设计使然。水印只是为了告诉你文本是否是由带水印的模型生成的，而不是告诉你这些想法是否来自人工智能或类似的东西。

children.author: kergonath
children.textRawHtml:
> It is also in the AI companies' own best interest to be able to detect AI generated text so that they can avoid training on it

It’s also in their interest to demonstrate that they can be trusted and to show that they at least pay lip service to limit the obvious downsides of the tools they are selling. The use cases they sell to mainstream audiences are not affected by detection tools. The point of having a LLM do the work for you is that the work is done, and reliably. It does not matter if it is done by a LLM, and most of the time it is obvious anyway.

证明自己可以被信任，并表明他们至少在口头上承诺限制他们所销售的工具的明显缺点，这也符合他们的利益。他们向主流受众销售的用例不受检测工具的影响。让法学硕士为您做工作的重点是工作已经完成，并且可靠。是否由 LLM 完成并不重要，而且大多数时候无论如何都是显而易见的。

children.author: ddalex
children.textRawHtml:
Probably they bias the RNG for selecting the next token. This can be done practically in a lot of ways, including during training.

I suspect the signal will be significantly under the noise floor, so it's not detectable if you don't know exactly what to look for, but certainly you can submit more information then the textual contents.
children.textZhHtml:
可能他们会偏向 RNG 选择下一个代币。这实际上可以通过多种方式完成，包括在训练期间。

我怀疑信号将明显低于本底噪声，因此如果您不确切知道要寻找什么，则无法检测到该信号，但您当然可以提交比文本内容更多的信息。

children.author: vintermann
children.textRawHtml: But if the user's prompt is in the context, you don't know exactly what the RNG chooses between. I don't know what trick they use to get past that, but it seems impossible to get by it in the general case (i.e. if the prompt can be anything) and you'll probably quickly compromise quality if you try.
children.textZhHtml: 但是如果用户的提示是在上下文中，你就无法确切知道 RNG 在什么之间进行选择。我不知道他们用什么技巧来克服这个问题，但在一般情况下似乎不可能克服它（即，如果提示可以是任何东西），如果你尝试的话，你可能很快就会妥协质量。

children.author: Majromax
children.textRawHtml:
A reasonable guess about the algorithm is 'A Watermark for Large Language Models' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10226). The idea is that each generated token (or bigram) seeds a strong PRNG that splits the vocabulary into a 'green' and 'red' set. The sampler then tries to select a 'green' next-token for generation.

After-the-fact checking only needs the vocabulary splitter, which is independent of the LLM. Over a sufficiently large text non-watermarked text would expect to use green and red tokens with the baseline probability, and that difference can easily become statistically significant over sufficiently long texts.

The basic algorithm has obvious knobs to tune, among them the initial ratio of red to green tokens and how hard the sampler tries to pick a green token. These would balance fidelity to the original distribution against watermark detectability (minimum required content length for statistical power).
children.textZhHtml:
对该算法的合理猜测是“大型语言模型的水印”(https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10226)。 这个想法是，每个生成的标记（或二元组）都会播种一个强大的 PRNG，将词汇表分为“绿色”和“红色”集。 然后，采样器尝试选择一个“绿色”的下一个令牌进行生成。

事后检查只需要词汇分割器，它独立于 LLM。 在足够大的文本上，无水印文本将期望使用具有基线概率的绿色和红色标记，并且在足够长的文本上，这种差异很容易变得具有统计显着性。

基本算法有明显的旋钮需要调整，其中包括红色与绿色标记的初始比率以及采样器尝试选择绿色标记的难度。 这些将平衡原始分布的保真度与水印可检测性（统计能力所需的最小内容长度）。
